note:
R98 - gen7 `.ast` stream framing on the ARCHIVE-BACKED titles the R91 loose-tree census omitted (25 September direction audit,
"extend ABKC / AST framing to the archive-backed titles ... using their own member hashes"): PS3 NHL 09 / 10 / 12 / 13 and X360 NHL 09.
Every `.abk` and `.ast` is taken as the exact archive member (BIG4 or EB listing from the R82 lister; wrapper = stored / RefPack /
chunkzip / chunklzx recorded per member, SHA-256 of the stored and of the decoded bytes), never a substituted loose sibling; where a
loose copy also exists (X360 NHL 09) it is listed as a second copy with its own hash and framed separately if its bytes differ.

Per bank member: R82 `abk_table` -> R89 `parse_tree` (the bank tree on an archived bank is itself a new measurement: refusals are
recorded, not forced) -> R91 `bank_streams` (stream entries with `.ast` offsets) -> R91 `analyse_ast` on the matching `.ast` member
(same stem; every copy in every archive is enumerated; the copy whose S10S id equals the bank's 0x2c word is used, others listed).
The R91 grammar, per-stream tests S1-S8 and the consumed-bytes accounting are reused unchanged (import), so a refusal here is a
refusal of the same grammar, and a pass is the same pass. Controls (R91 `controls`) run once per platform on `crowds` in memory
on a copy of the decoded member bytes (the archive itself is never written; the member is re-decoded afterwards and its hash
compared).
Separation kept: this is STRUCTURAL enumeration; representative decode tests are a separate probe (r99 / r92 route) and are not
implied by a `framed` status. Residuals (refused / unsupported-codec / no `.ast` copy / undecodable wrapper) are listed per member.
Usage: python r98_ast_framing_archived.py <out.json> [--trees a,b] [--summary FILE.jsonl] [--no-controls] [--max-member-mb N]
